He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]] and was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. ==High school career== In his [[freshman]] season in 2016–17, Cooper averaged 16 points and 4.4 assists per game, leading [[McEachern High School]] in [[Powder Springs, Georgia]] to a 29–1 record and an appearance in the [[Georgia High School Association]] (GHSA) Class 7A state semifinals. The following year, he led the Indians to a state quarterfinals appearance while posting a 26–3 record.{{cite news |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/06/06/hoop-with-coop-a-point-guard-from-georgia-gives-the-world-an-introduction/ |title=Hoop With Coop: A Point Guard from Georgia Gives The World An Introduction |first=David |last=Cordova |publisher=Dave's Joint |date=June 6, 2018 |access-date=July 27, 2019}} He received considerable media attention in December 2017 for his 42-point performance against [[Jahvon Quinerly]] and nationally ranked [[Hudson Catholic Regional High School]] in the quarterfinals of the [[City of Palms Classic]]. He scored the game-winning buzzer-beater in an 83–81 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] victory.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/FvJAXXeXyEq2SZgow2GNEw/sharife-coopers-42-point-performance-highlights-early-going-at-city-of-palms-classic.htm|title=Sharife Cooper's 42-point performance highlights early going at City of Palms Classic|first=Lynden|last=Ostrander|publisher=MaxPreps|date=December 21, 2017|access-date=July 27, 2019}}{{cite news|url=https://hoopseen.com/news/event/201712/cooper-has-epic-outing-ot-mceachern-win|title=Cooper Has Epic Outing in OT McEachern Win|first=Justin|last=Young|publisher=HoopSeen|date=December 20, 2017|access-date=July 27, 2019}} As a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] in 2018–19, Cooper led McEachern to a perfect 32–0 record and the first state title in school history while averaging 27.2 points, 8.1 assists, 5.6 rebounds and 4.3 steals per game. In the title-game win over [[Meadowcreek High School|Meadowcreek]], he scored 20 points and dished four assists as McEachern finished ranked No. 1 in three national polls.{{cite news|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/aaaaaaa-basketball-blog-mceachern-westlake-finish-unbeaten-nationally-ranked/xC00FOEfhm6RguahaYHm0H/|title=AAAAAAA basketball blog: McEachern, Westlake finish unbeaten, nationally ranked|first=Todd|last=Holcomb|publisher=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=July 28, 2019}} He picked up [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors at several tournaments, including the City of Palms Classic and Tournament of Champions.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/hiEtJCTmEUuugDTFsLy1Ng/sharife-cooper-leads-race-for-high-school-basketball-player-of-the-year-honors.htm|title=Sharife Cooper leads race for high school consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]], Cooper was considered one of the top prospects in his class. On September 27, 2019, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], becoming the highest-ranked recruit and the second five-star recruit in program history.{{cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |title=5-star point guard Sharife Cooper commits to Auburn |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2019/09/5-star-point-guard-sharife-cooper-commits-to-auburn.html |website=AL.com |access-date=September 27, 2019 |date=September 27, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Sharife Cooper | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Powder Springs, GA]] | highschool = [[McEachern High School|McEachern]] (GA) | feet = 6 | inches = 0 | weight = 160 | 40 = | commitdate = September 27, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 94 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Auburn 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Auburn Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = auburn | scout s = | espn schoolid = 2 | 247 overall = 27 | rivals overall = 22 | espn overall = 20 | accessdate = October 14, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Cooper missed the first 12 games of his freshman season due to a [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] investigation into his eligibility. During that time, he explored professional options.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Auburn Tigers freshman Sharife Cooper cleared by NCAA, to make debut Saturday |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30679440 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=January 9, 2021}} On January 9, 2021, he made his Auburn debut, recording 26 points, nine assists and four rebounds in a 94–90 loss to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web |last=Han |first=Giana |title=Sharife Cooper's debut encouraging for Auburn despite loss |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2021/01/sharife-coopers-debut-encouraging-for-auburn-despite-loss.html |website=[[AL.com]] |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=January 9, 2021}} Four days later, Cooper posted a season-high 28 points, 12 assists and five rebounds in a 95–77 win over [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]].{{cite web |title=Cooper dominant again as Auburn beats Georgia 95–77 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258746 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=January 13, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 20.2 points, 8.1 assists and 4.3 rebounds per game through 12 appearances, earning [[Southeastern Conference]] All-Freshman Team honors. On April 2, 2021, Cooper declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |title=Auburn's Sharife Cooper to enter NBA draft, hire agent |url=https://www.nba.com/news/auburns-sharife-cooper-to-enter-nba-draft-hire-agent |website=NBA.com |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=April 2, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2021–2022)=== Cooper was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 48th pick by the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite news|last=Vivlamore|first=Chris|title=Driveway competition just the way for Sharife Cooper to start NBA career|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-hawks/driveway-competition-just-the-way-for-sharife-cooper-to-start-nba-career/GBY36B243RDGLEAUIBQTLJCRR4/|work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=August 2, 2021}} On August 5, 2021, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Hawks, splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign 2021 Draft Picks Jalen Johnson and Sharife Cooper|url=https://www.NBA.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-2021-draft-picks-jalen-johnson-and-sharife-cooper|website=NBA.com|date=August 5, 2021|access-date=August 5, 2021}} He played for the Hawks in the [[2021 NBA Summer League]], recording 11 points on 5–11 shooting, and 6 assists in 28 minutes at his debut in a 85–83 loss against the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Atlanta Hawks Aug 8, 2021 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-atl-1522100001/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 8, 2021}} Cooper made his NBA debut in the Hawks' season opener against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], going 0-for-3 from the field in a 113–87 win.{{Cite web |title=Dallas Mavericks vs Atlanta Hawks Oct 21, 2021 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/dal-vs-atl-0022100014/box-score |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=NBA.com}} Cooper joined the Hawks' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612737/hawks |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=NBA.com}} On July 22, 2022, Cooper re-signed with the Hawks on another two-way deal.{{Cite web |title=Hawks Re-Sign Sharife Cooper To Two-Way Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/07/hawks-re-sign-sharife-cooper-to-two-way-deal.html |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=Hoops Rumors |date=July 22, 2022 |last=Adams|first=Luke}} He was waived three days later.{{Cite web |date=2022-07-25 |title=Atlanta Hawks request waivers on 2021 second-round pick Sharife Cooper |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34294774 |access-date=2026-02-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}} ===Cleveland Charge (2022–2024)=== On September 20, 2022, Cooper signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]],{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Sharife Cooper Signs Camp Deal With Cavs|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/09/sharife-cooper-to-sign-camp-deal-with-cavs.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 20, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2023}} but was waived on October 15.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Five Players|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-player-waiving-221015|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2023}} On October 24, he joined the [[Cleveland Charge]]'s training camp roster.{{cite web|title=Charge 2022 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2022-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} Cooper was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}} In July 2023, Cooper joined the Cleveland Cavaliers for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]] and on September 13, 2023, he re-signed with the Cavaliers.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Sharife Cooper, Pete Nance, and Justin Powell to Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-training-camp-signings-230913|website=NBA.com|date=September 13, 2023|access-date=September 13, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 21{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Cavaliers Waive Seven Players|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/cavaliers-waive-seven-players.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} and one week later re-signed with the Charge.{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} On February 26, 2024, Cooper signed a 10-day contract with the Cavaliers,{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Sharife Cooper to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-sharife-cooper-signing-240226|website=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2024|access-date=February 26, 2024}} although he failed to make an appearance. On March 7, he returned to the Charge.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Cleveland Charge Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Cleveland-Charge/34/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 7, 2024}} ===Liaoning Flying Leopards (2024)=== On April 1, 2024, Cooper signed with the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{cite news|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Sharife Cooper signs with Liaoning Flying Leopards|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/sharife-cooper-signs-with-liaoning-flying-leopards/|newspaper=Sportando|date=April 2, 2024|access-date=April 2, 2024}} He helped the Flying Leopards win the 2024 CBA championship, recording 22 points, nine assists and six rebounds off the bench in their title-clinching Game 4 victory over the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]].{{cite news|url=http://www.china.org.cn/sports/2024-05/23/content_117207137.htm|title=Liaoning clinch third consecutive CBA title|website=[[China.org.cn]]|date=May 23, 2024|access-date=May 23, 2024}}
